tasks.sciEvidence: A concrete definition gives a directed propagation-path geometrical line with no physical width. Straightness is limited to the homogeneous-medium approximation; rays, finite beams and visible scattering traces are distinguished.
tasks.zhenEvidence: Definition, direction arrow, straight-line limitation and scattering qualification correspond in both languages.

tasks.sciEvidence: Luminous flux is defined as specified visual-response-weighted optical radiant power, in lm. It is explicitly separated from unweighted watts, subjective brightness, cd and lx.
tasks.zhenEvidence: Both retain prescribed spectral weighting, energy-transfer rate, lumen and the same three distinctions; the shorter English first paragraph does not omit a separate physical claim.

tasks.sciEvidence: Specifies direction and solid angle, I=dPhi/dOmega, and cd=lm/sr. Finite Phi/Omega is directional intensity only under angular uniformity; otherwise it is the regional mean. A geometric point source does not imply isotropy.
tasks.zhenEvidence: Direction, local derivative, solid-angle unit, conditional finite ratio, mean interpretation and no inferred isotropy correspond exactly.

tasks.sciEvidence: Answers all three factors with directional I, distance R and angle to normal: E=I cos(alpha)/R^2. Includes cd/m/lx, small unobstructed front-facing patch, fixed-other-conditions proportionalities, per-source addition and separate reflected/background light.
tasks.zhenEvidence: The factor list, angle range, normal rather than plane, direct-light conditions, units and summation have the same scope.

tasks.sciEvidence: Gives the actual side-view prediction: beam not visible from the front-wall hole when visible scattering is negligible and the eye is off the direct transit path. Explains light reaching the eye and distinguishes scattering, reflective surfaces, outgoing-path viewing and illuminated edges.
tasks.zhenEvidence: The three wall-hole roles, conditional negative prediction and all exceptions match. Neither says clean air has exactly zero scattering.

tasks.sciEvidence: Predicts a partial solar disk for a sun-visible observer in the Moon's penumbra. Finite solar angular diameter explains blocked and unblocked paths; lunar eclipse and a claim about all Earth observers are excluded.
tasks.zhenEvidence: Both specify the same observer location, partial solar eclipse, finite disk and shadow ownership.

tasks.sciEvidence: Explains Alex's specific rooftops/trees/clothes scene using a dark room, small two-direction aperture, straight-ray mapping, vertical and horizontal inversion, and diffuse wall reflection. Object colors explain the colored image; a literal separated spectrum would need an unspecified mechanism. Long-slit blur is explicitly distinguished.
tasks.zhenEvidence: Alex, the complete scene, both inversion directions, wall-to-eye light, scene color versus spectrum and the two-transverse-dimensions condition correspond.
tasks.scopeLimit: PASS for the explicitly conditional scene-image explanation, not proof of a disperser, literal spectrum or arbitrary-slit clarity.

tasks.sciEvidence: Finite streetlamp emitter produces displaced shadow edges and penumbra. Feet near the receiving ground have smaller displacement than the head. A mere brightness-distance explanation is rejected; the ideal-point-source and other-light contrast limits are separate.
tasks.zhenEvidence: Both preserve finite emitter, feet/head receiving-surface geometry, edge blur, ideal limit and secondary contrast effects.

tasks.sciEvidence: Concrete distances 1.6 m from 80 cd and 2.0 m from 125 cd, positive-distance ratio 4/5, and 31.25 lx match the existing independent derivation/results. Opposite rays/faces give equal incidence angles: a positive common cosine cancels for non-grazing tilt; at 90 degrees both sides are zero and location is not unique. Local screen-center and direct-light assumptions are stated.
tasks.zhenEvidence: Distances are assigned to the same sources, both printed requests are answered, and normal/tilted illumination, strict cosine range, zero-factor degeneracy and neglected effects match.
tasks.numericComparison: Existing d280 /solutions/9/derivation and /derivedResults compared; no arithmetic rerun.

tasks.sciEvidence: Retains h=3 m, l=4 m and 200 cd per relevant direction. Under each lamp it includes own 200/9 lx plus the other's oblique 4.8 lx, total 1216/45 lx (~27.0222). Under midpoint it includes both 600/(13 sqrt(13)) contributions, total 1200/(13 sqrt(13)) lx (~25.6015). Distances and normal-based cosines match d280; specified ceiling/wall reflections are excluded.
